### Investment Memo: ADBE — October 18, 2026

**Verdict**: BUY | Conviction: **Medium**
**Price Target**: $330 (~35% upside from current $245.20)
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months, tranche entry

**Investment Thesis**
Adobe is a 89%-gross-margin, ~48%-ROIC franchise trading at ~10x forward earnings and a ~10% FCF yield because the market has priced it as an AI casualty. The forensic evidence rejects that framing: accounting is clean, cash conversion is 1.41x, the balance sheet is effectively net-debt-free, revenue is *re-accelerating* (+13% Q3 FY26), and the buyback retires ~10% of shares annually — meaning per-share value compounds even with zero growth. The bear case (seat-model disruption) is legitimate but is a 2027–2030 terminal-value question already more than reflected in a multiple that has compressed ~60%; the burden of proof has shifted to the bears. Conviction is capped at Medium by genuinely weak governance, a hostile real-rate path, and deteriorating near-term demand signals.

**Key Findings by Domain**
- **Macro & Sector**: Macro is *unfavourable* — 10Y real yield 2.78% (+87bp in 5 months), ~50% October hike odds; this pressures the multiple, not the business (net cash, negligible refinancing risk). Sector is in an AI-driven de-rating with extreme dispersion: ADBE is #1 on gross margin (89.1%) and operating margin (35.7%) among peers, #2-last on growth (12.5% vs ~17.5% median), and cheapest at 3.6x sales — priced for stagnation.
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: Medium risk, low materiality. DOJ/ROSCA settled ($150M + injunction on cancellation flows); **UK CMA probe into the same conduct is live**; EU AI Act obligations now apply to 27% of revenue. Worst case is a low-single-digit EPS drag — an irritant, not thesis-defining.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Value**: Financial quality 9/10; FCF conversion 138%; blended intrinsic value ~**$392** (25/45/30 weighting of $605/$385/$225 scenarios) — a ~37% discount. Price implies 0–1% perpetual FCF growth. Moat rated **Narrow (contested)**, down from Wide — the key honest uncertainty.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Growth**: Rule of 40 = **52** at 10.0x forward P/E; FY26 guide raised twice; AI-first ARR +150% to >$650M (but only ~2.4% of base). Fair value $300–330. Deceleration to ~9% by FY27 and negative long-dated revisions cap this at a value-plus-optionality call, not a compounder call.
- **Quantitative Signals**: **Value #1/6 and Quality #1/6** simultaneously in the software comp set — a rare double. But momentum middling (+11.8% vs CRM +46.7%), Sharpe −0.29, MDD −42%, revisions −6.5% (thin 6-analyst sample). R² vs SPY of 0.0075 means returns are essentially pure idiosyncratic risk.
- **Financial Risk**: Split rating. Credit **LOW** (0.01x net leverage, 33x coverage, A+, Z-score 4.35); equity **HIGH** (37–44% vol, −67% 3y max drawdown). Watch: FY25 buybacks ($11.28B) exceeded FCF ($9.85B); goodwill/intangibles of $13.35B = 115% of book equity is a Digital Experience impairment risk.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: **HIGH** — the binding constraint. Say-on-pay passed at just **50.65%**; CEO *and* CFO seats simultaneously in transition (Narayen → Chakravarthy Dec 1, interim CFO); Narayen retains Board Chair; ~$45M of insider selling with **zero insider buying** at multi-year lows; AI training-data class actions active.
- **ESG**: Average. E a sector leader (SBTi net-zero); S damaged by the regulator-confirmed consumer-protection failure (the injunction permanently removes friction-based retention — model consumer net adds conservatively); G weak in practice. Firefly's commercially-safe training data and C2PA provenance work is an under-appreciated ESG *asset* supporting pricing power.
- **Alternative Data**: **Bearish near-term.** Creative Cloud/Photoshop search interest −21% to −25% sequentially with a counter-seasonal failure to recover into fall; Canva captured the recovery (+61% off July low) while Firefly mindshare fell −62% from peak; EPS beat magnitude compressing (3.24% → 2.41% → 0.82%). Revenue/ARR quality tracking below consensus into the Dec 9 print; EPS roughly in-line.
- **Short / Contrarian View**: **Short thesis rejected at $245.** M-Score −2.85, negative accruals four years running — one of the cleanest large-cap profiles reviewed; "anyone shorting ADBE on an accounting thesis is shorting the wrong thing." The short was right at $440–500; it has been paid. Downside from here requires an actual *revenue decline*, not deceleration. Notable forensic flags: ARR growth (10.9%) now trails revenue growth (12.0%), and five quarters of ~10.5% growth *through price increases* implies weak underlying unit growth.

**Bull Case**
- Valuation dislocation: ~10x FY26E EPS / ~10.6x FCF for 89% gross margins, 41% FCF margins, 47.7% ROIC — even the slow-erosion DCF scenario is worth ~$385.
- Self-correcting mechanism: a ~10%-of-market-cap annual buyback at ~10x cash flow compounds per-share value at low-double-digit rates with *no* growth and *no* re-rating required.
- AI optionality is free: AI-first ARR +150% YoY, NVIDIA partnership, Firefly's commercially-safe moat, and Q3's +13% re-acceleration directly refute "AI is already eating Adobe."

**Bear Case**
- Seat-model disruption: AI collapses the prosumer/casual creation tier (Canva, Figma, OpenAI); alt data shows Adobe losing the demand-funnel recovery to Canva *now*, and per-seat pricing is structurally mismatched with AI-driven seat compression.
- Quality-of-growth deterioration: ARR < revenue growth, price increases masking unit weakness, beat magnitude decaying, FY27 consensus already below FY26 — the leading indicators all point the wrong way.
- Governance + macro compound: a dual C-suite vacuum with a 50.65% say-on-pay vote executes the AI pivot while real yields rise 87bp-per-five-months; two hikes + 3% real yield puts the $195 June low back in play.

**Key Risks**
1. Sustained ARR deceleration below 8% or gross margin below 88% — the two hardest thesis breaks (currently 10.2% guided / 89.3%).
2. Real-rate shock: Fed hikes Oct + Dec → 10Y real >3% → $195 retest, $170s below.
3. Digital Experience impairment of the $13.35B goodwill/intangible stack.
4. Capital allocation: debt-funded buybacks at poor prices (~$5B destroyed buying at ~$400 avg in FY25), or an outsider CEO overpaying for an AI asset (Figma 2.0).
5. UK CMA adverse finding; AI copyright litigation escalation; negative estimate revisions broadening.

**Portfolio Construction Note**
**Initiate 1.0% now; path to 2.0%; hard cap 3.0%.** Add +0.5% post-Dec-9 *only if* FY27 guide ≥9% and ending ARR ≥9.5% — do not pre-position into a "sell-the-beat" regime; add +0.5% at $195–215 only with gross margin ≥88%. Hard stop $188 (max loss 0.46% of NAV at target size). Exit regardless of price on: deferred revenue growth < revenue growth, ARR <8%, GM <88%, DX impairment, or a second senior finance departure. Trim one-third at $350, another at $390–400. ADBE correlates 0.72–0.77 with CRM/NOW/INTU — it counts against the **software-cluster bucket, not as a diversifier**; cut sizing 25% if the book already holds SaaS peers. **Do not beta-hedge** (1y beta 0.29 vs vendor 1.42, R² 0.0075 — the hedge won't track); size on 44% total vol. Cheap and improving are different things — ADBE is the former and not yet the latter; own it small, get paid to wait via the buyback, and let the ARR line dictate whether this becomes 3% or an exit.

*Data gaps flagged: market cap reported as both $95.4B (389M sh) and $104.7B (427M diluted) — FCF yield 9.4–10.3% either way; FY29→FY30 consensus EPS curve internally inconsistent (disregarded); 10-K litigation footnotes unverified (SEC access blocked); web/app-traffic and job-posting alt-data feeds unavailable.*

# ADBE — Portfolio Construction Recommendation

**Price $245.20 (close 16-Oct-26) · Mkt cap $104.7B (427M diluted) · Q4 FY26 earnings 9-Dec-26 · Composite Action: INITIATE (1.0% starter → 2.0% target, 3.0% cap)**

---

## 1. Agent Conviction Summary Table

| Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Value** | BUY (tranches) | **High** | Blended IV **$392** (25/45/30: $605 / $385 / $225) = 37% discount; ROIC 47.7%, FCF conversion 138%; price implies 0–1% perpetual FCF growth |
| **Quant** | BUY (not Strong) | **High (on factors), Low (on timing)** | **Value #1/6 and Quality #1/6** simultaneously; R² vs SPY **0.0075** — returns are pure idiosyncratic; Sharpe −0.69, Sortino −0.46, MDD −42% |
| **Short Analyst** | **NO EDGE — reject short** | **High** | M-score −2.85, accruals −9.8%, cash conversion 1.41x, F-score 7/9. **No fraud.** Bear case is consensus, not insight |
| **Sector** | NEUTRAL sector / ADBE = contrarian value | Medium | #1 gross margin (89.1%) and op margin (35.7%), **#2-last on growth** (12.5% vs 17.5% median), cheapest at 3.6x sales / 55% P/E discount |
| **Fin Risk** | MODERATE (split rating) | High | Credit **LOW** (0.01x net leverage, 33x coverage, A+); Equity **HIGH** (37–44% vol, −67% 3y MDD); buybacks $11.28B vs FCF $9.85B |
| **Growth** | BUY (moderate) | Medium | Rule of 40 = 52 at **10.0x fwd P/E**; but Firefly search −62%, Canva recovering, FCF margin 47%→44%; fair value $300–330 |
| **Geo Legal** | MEDIUM risk | High (low impact) | DOJ settled $150M + injunction; **UK CMA probe live**; EU AI Act live; low-single-digit % EPS drag — *not thesis-defining* |
| **ESG** | AVERAGE / mildly negative | Medium | Injunction permanently removes friction-based retention; C2PA/Firefly commercial-safety is a genuine asset |
| **Alt Data** | **BEARISH** | Medium | Creative Cloud search **−25% sequential**, counter-seasonal (no fall recovery); Canva +61% off July low; beat magnitude 3.24%→2.41%→**0.82%** |
| **Macro** | **UNFAVOURABLE** | High | **10Y real yield 2.78%, +87bp in 5 months**; ~50% Oct hike odds; bear case = $195 retest, $170s |
| **Non-Fin Risk** | **HIGH** | High | Say-on-pay **50.65%**; CEO *and* CFO vacancies concurrent; Narayen stays Board Chair; AI-training class actions (~200k books); $45M insider selling, **zero buying** |

## 2. Consensus Assessment: **MEDIUM (fundamentals) / SPLIT (timing)**

There is unusually strong agreement on *what* Adobe is: **four independent agents (Value, Quant, Short, Fin Risk) converge on "statistically cheap, genuinely high-quality, clean accounting."** The short-seller — whose job is to find fraud — explicitly rejected the short at this price. That is the highest-value signal in the file and it removes the one category of risk that would override a valuation call.

There is equally strong agreement on *near-term direction*: Alt Data, Quant (revisions −6.5%), Short (ARR 10.9% < revenue 12.0%), and Growth (alt-data) all say the leading indicators are deteriorating **now**.

These are not contradictory. **The market is pricing the deterioration, and more than pricing it.** Where agents genuinely split is the one question that determines terminal value: *is AI compressing Adobe's seat economics permanently?* Sector says eroding; Short says a 2027–2030 problem, not a 2026 one; Value says honestly unresolved. Record **89.3% gross margin** is the strongest single fact against the bear case — if pricing power were cracking, it would show there first.

**Conflict resolution applied:** Non-Fin's HIGH governance rating is the binding constraint, not the valuation. I discount the bull case for a 50.65% say-on-pay vote, a dual C-suite vacuum, and active IP litigation — none of which the three bull agents weight at all. That discount is what caps sizing below what the value math alone would support.

## 3. Position Sizing Recommendation: **2.0% of portfolio target (1.0% now; hard cap 3.0%)**

**Kelly input, then discounted.** With a 55% probability of working, +44% to $353 (90% of blended IV) and −23% to the stop, b = 1.91 → Kelly = (0.55×1.91 − 0.45)/1.91 = **31%**. Quarter-Kelly ≈ 7.8%. That is unusable for a single name because the IV range is **$225–$605** — terminal value is 60%+ of the DCF, so the probability estimate is not reliable enough to size off. Applying a conviction discount for (i) unresolved terminal value, (ii) HIGH governance risk, (iii) hostile real-rate path, (iv) median sell-side target of **$257.50 — only 5% above spot** → **2.0% target, 3.0% cap.**

**Risk budget check:** at 44.4% vol, 2.0% of NAV contributes **0.89% of portfolio volatility** — roughly **5.9% in SPY-equivalent risk** (44.4/15 ≈ 3.0x). The 3.0% cap therefore consumes ~8.8% of market-equivalent risk budget, which is the most a single idio-cratic name of unresolved terminal value should command.

## 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

- **Sector concentration — ADDITIVE, not diversifying.** Correlations of **CRM 0.76, NOW 0.77, INTU 0.72** confirm ADBE is a fifth position in the *same SaaS cluster*, not a diversifier. Only MSFT (0.41) and SPY (**0.086**) are lowly correlated. **Rule: ADBE counts against the software-cluster bucket, not standalone.** Cap total application-software exposure at 12–15%; if the book already holds CRM/NOW/INTU, cut this sizing by 25%.
- **Factor exposure — deliberate, and it will hurt.** This adds a **value + quality** bet against a **momentum-led** peer set (CRM +46.7%, MSFT +28.7%, NOW +24.5% vs ADBE +11.8%) with negative revisions. Expect tracking error if momentum persists. Size accordingly — do not let a factor bet masquerade as a stock pick.
- **Beta is unhedgeable.** 1y beta **0.291** (R² 0.0075) vs vendor 1.415 — irreconcilable. **Do not beta- or index-hedge this position**; the hedge will not track. Size on total volatility (44.4%), never beta-adjusted.
- **Correlation paradox:** near-zero correlation to SPY (0.086) makes ADBE a *diversifier at the index level* and a *concentrator at the sector level*. Net effect in a software-heavy book: concentration.

## 5. Entry Strategy: **SCALE-IN — 1.0% now, do not add into 9-Dec**

Price is mid-range, not a capitulation low: **$190.12 low (18-Jun) → $292.79 (31-Aug, +54%) → $245.20 (−16%)**. At 10.0x FY26E EPS and 10.6x P/FCF the entry is valuation-supported but not technically extreme.

- **Tranche 1 — now: 1.0% at ~$245.**
- **Tranche 2 — +0.5% on the 9-Dec print *only if* FY27 guide ≥9% and ending ARR ≥9.5%.** Do not pre-position into this catalyst: the current regime is "sell the beat" (a Q2 revenue beat was met with a **−12.6% two-day gap**), so event risk is negatively skewed.
- **Tranche 3 — +0.5% at $195–215 *if* gross margin ≥88% and ARR ≥9%.** Price weakness with intact fundamentals is the add; price weakness with ARR <8% is the exit.
- **Ceiling discipline:** if price runs to $320+ without ARR confirmation, **hold at 1.0%** — do not chase a re-rating.

## 6. Risk Management Rules

**Hard stop: $188 (close basis, below the $190.12 June low) = −23%.** A tighter stop is noise on a 44%-vol name; a wider one breaches the risk budget. Max loss at target size: **0.46% of NAV.**

**Thesis invalidation — exit regardless of price, in priority order** (the first two are earliest-warning, per Short Analyst):
1. **Deferred revenue growth < revenue growth** (billings lead revenue — monitor first)
2. **Revenue growth < ARR growth for two consecutive quarters** (non-recurring mix rising)
3. **Ending ARR growth < 8%** — the single hardest invalidation
4. **Gross margin < 88%** — the first true pricing-power crack (currently 89.3%)
5. **Digital Experience organic growth negative, or any goodwill impairment** ($13.35B = 115% of book equity)
6. **Second senior finance departure**, or an outsider CEO overpaying for an AI asset (Figma 2.0)
7. **Buybacks resumed above $300 funded with incremental debt** — the EPS-defence tell

**Trim triggers:** trim **one-third at $350** (≈90% of $392 blended IV); a second third at **$390–400** (full blended IV). Retain the residual as a compounding position while ARR ≥9% — the buyback retires ~10% of shares annually at these prices, so per-share value compounds without a re-rating.

**Rebalance:** trim back to 2.5% if appreciation takes the position above 3.5% of NAV without fundamental confirmation.

**Proof window:** hold at 1.0% maximum until **four consecutive quarters** confirm ARR ≥9%, AI-first ARR converting to *net-new* revenue (not credit repricing), and buybacks ≥7% of shares annually.

## 7. Final Portfolio Action: **INITIATE — 1.0% starter, path to 2.0%, cap 3.0%**

**Rationale.** This is the rare configuration where the value, quality and forensic agents agree *and* the short-seller has abandoned the short. At ~10x forward earnings, 10.6x FCF and 14.7x GAAP with 89% gross margins, a fortress balance sheet and a buyback retiring 10% of shares a year, the downside requires an actual *revenue decline* — not deceleration. But the median sell-side target sits 5% above spot, governance is genuinely weak, real yields are rising 87bp per five months, and the demand data is deteriorating counter-seasonally. **Cheap and improving are different things; ADBE is the former and not yet the latter.** Therefore: own it small, get paid to wait via the buyback, and let the 9-Dec print and the ARR line — not the share price — dictate whether this becomes a 3% position or an exit.

**Two data gaps to flag for the memo:** (1) market cap is reported as both $95.4B (389M shares) and $104.7B (427M diluted) — FCF yield is 10.3% or 9.4% depending on basis, high either way; (2) the FY2029/FY2030 consensus EPS curve is internally inconsistent ($37.26 → $34.84 on 6 analysts) and I have disregarded it — anchor only on FY26E $24.48 and FY27E $27.73.

# Sector Brief — Technology / Software – Application (ADBE)

## 1. Sector Overview

Adobe sits in **application software**, specifically two adjacent sub-markets: **creative/document productivity** (Digital Media — Creative Cloud, Document Cloud) and **digital experience / marketing & analytics software** (Digital Experience — AEP, GenStudio, Analytics). The sub-sector is a **high-gross-margin (75–92%), subscription/recurring-revenue industry** now mid-transition from **seat-based to consumption/AI-outcome-based pricing**. Market structure is **moderately concentrated but fragmenting at the edges**: Microsoft, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Intuit, Autodesk and Adobe anchor the enterprise side, while generative-AI-native entrants (Figma — now public — Canva, OpenAI, Google, Runway) attack the low end and the "creation" workflow. The sector is **not early-cycle**; it is a **mature-growth industry undergoing an AI-driven re-platforming**, which has produced unusually wide dispersion in multiples: AI-perceived winners (NOW 11.1x sales, MSFT 11.8x, FIG 9.9x) trade at 3–4x the multiples of perceived AI losers.

**Cycle position: late mature-growth, in a de-rating phase.** Revenue growth for large-cap application software has settled into a **~10–20% band** (peer median ~17.5%), and the market is repricing duration risk as AI both *expands* the addressable market and *compresses* per-seat monetisation. Adobe's own TTM revenue growth (**+12.5% 9M FY26**, Q3 FY26 **+13% YoY**) is at the *low end* of that band yet the stock has de-rated hardest.

## 2. Key Tailwinds

- **AI monetisation is inflecting, not cannibalising (so far).** Q3 FY26: record revenue **$6.76B (+13% YoY)**, **AI-first ARR +150% YoY**, and the **1 billion MAU** milestone; FY26 guidance *raised* to **$26.5–26.6B revenue / $24.35–24.45 non-GAAP EPS**. The NVIDIA partnership (Photoshop, Premiere, Substance 3D, agentic creation) lowers inference cost and improves speed-to-output.
- **Structural content demand.** Every enterprise is becoming a content business — marketing personalisation, commerce, short-form video. Adobe's own data shows **US holiday online spend of $275.1B (+6.7% YoY)** — a direct proxy for the digital-content/commerce volume that feeds both Digital Media and Digital Experience demand.
- **Best-in-class unit economics + a discounted multiple.** **89.1% TTM gross margin** and **35.7% TTM operating margin** are top-decile versus peers, with heavy recurring revenue and strong FCF. At **~3.6x forward sales / ~10x FY26 non-GAAP EPS**, the market is pricing structural decline, not 12–13% growth with 36% margins — an asymmetry if AI fears prove overdone.

## 3. Key Headwinds

- **Barriers to entry are collapsing at the low end.** Generative AI removes the tooling-skills moat that protected Creative Cloud for two decades. Figma (**+41% growth**, 82% GM) and Canva are taking collaborative/prosumer design; OpenAI/Google image-video generation is taking casual creation. **Buyer power is rising** (monthly subs, low consumer switching costs), and Adobe's ~12–13% growth versus 26–41% for AI-native peers signals **share loss in the fastest-growing pockets**.
- **Seat-based model risk / pricing power compression.** If AI agents do the work of multiple seats, per-seat ARR faces a structural ceiling. Adobe must convert units→consumption (credits, Firefly generations) without revenue leakage — an unproven transition that keeps a sentiment discount on the name and drove an **analyst downgrade in Oct 2026**.
- **Margin pressure from AI inference + SBC.** Operating margin has already wobbled — **37.8% (Q1 FY26) → 33.8% (Q2) → 34.8% (Q3)**, versus 36.6% in FY25 — as compute costs rise. The **GAAP-vs-non-GAAP gap is large** (~$18 GAAP vs ~$24.40 non-GAAP EPS), so headline "10x earnings" is partly a stock-compensation artefact. FX is also a drag: **+13% reported vs +11% constant currency** in Q2 FY26.

## 4. Peer Comparison Table

| MSFT | 331.84 | +17.8% | 67.9% | 46.8% | 11.8x | 29.4x |
| CRM | 41.53 | +9.6% | 77.7% | 21.5% | 4.8x | 26.6x |
| NOW | 13.28 | +20.9% | 77.5% | 13.7% | 11.1x | 84.0x |
| INTU | 21.45 | +13.9% | 80.2% | 28.8% | 4.1x | 19.0x |
| ADSK | 7.21 | +17.5% | 92.3% | 21.9% | 7.0x | 44.6x |
| TEAM | 6.57 | +26.0% | 84.8% | 0.2% | 8.0x | n.m. |
| FIG | 1.06 | +41.0% | 82.4% | n.m. (neg.) | 9.9x | n.m. |
| **Peer median** | — | **~17.5%** | **80.2%** | **21.5%** | **8.0x** | **29.4x** |

**Read-across:** Adobe is **#1 on gross margin (89.1% vs 80.2% median), #1 on operating margin among profitable peers (35.7% vs 21.5% median), #2-last on growth (12.5% vs ~17.5% median), and cheapest on both P/S (55% discount) and P/E (55% discount).** Market-share momentum clearly sits with NOW/ADSK/TEAM/FIG (17–41% growth); CRM is the other large-cap decelerator (~9.6%).

**Price action confirms the de-rating:** ADBE **$245.20**, **−28.6% YoY** (from $343.72), **−31.9% below** its Oct-2025 high of $359.91, with a violent **−25% drawdown in June 2026** (peak-to-trough $259→$190). It has since recovered **+29% off the $190 low** — i.e. sentiment, not fundamentals, is the marginal driver.

## 5. Target Company's Competitive Position: **STRONG (but eroding relative to peers)**

- **Strengths:** Unmatched installed base and workflow entrenchment in professional creative and PDF/document standards; 1B MAU; 89% gross margin; enterprise DX cross-sell into the same CMO buyer; balance sheet and FCF to acquire capability (Semrush-class tuck-ins) and to fund buybacks (share count down ~5% YoY).
- **Weaknesses:** Lowest growth of the large-cap peer set; direct assault by Figma/Canva in design and by frontier model providers in generation; consumer/prosumer revenue base is the most AI-disruptable portion of application software; margin already compressing as AI compute costs land; GAAP earnings quality diluted by SBC.
- **Verdict:** **Strong franchise, average-to-weak momentum.** Adobe retains the widest moat and best economics in the peer group, but its **relative growth and pricing power are deteriorating** — the classic profile of a share donor in a re-platforming cycle. The valuation is the compensating variable: **~3.6x sales for an 89%-gross-margin, 36%-operating-margin, 12–13% grower** is priced for stagnation.

## 6. Sector Rating: **NEUTRAL**

Application software remains a **structurally attractive** industry (recurring revenue, 75–92% gross margins, secular content/automation demand), but it is in a **de-rating and business-model transition phase** in which **dispersion is extreme** — AI-perceived winners command 8–12x sales while perceived losers sit at 3–5x, regardless of current profitability. Input cost trends (AI inference compute, GPU/cloud pricing) are **inflationary for the first time in a decade**, and the seat-based pricing model is under credible threat. Recommend **market-weight the sector with a strong preference for AI-native revenue mix**; within it, Adobe is a **deep-value / contrarian recovery positioning rather than a momentum holding** — attractive *if and only if* AI-first ARR growth (+150% YoY) proves it can re-monetise its base faster than it loses seats.

*Data gaps: no HHI or explicit market-share series available in-feed; peer multiples are market-cap/latest-FY approximations (no EV bridge for net debt); TAM figures are company-estimated and not independently verified here.*

## 1. Business Quality Assessment — Moat Rating: **Narrow** (was Wide; now contested)

Adobe is three businesses with very different economics:

**Document Cloud (Acrobat/PDF) — Wide moat.** PDF is a de facto global standard; Acrobat sits inside corporate document workflows, e-signature, and compliance processes. This is a toll road. Switching costs are institutional, not just individual.

**Creative Cloud — Narrow and narrowing.** The 5-year evidence was excellent: 89% gross margins held across 2020–2025 (86.6% → 89.3%), pricing power exercised annually, and a subscriber base locked in by file formats, team libraries, plugin ecosystems, and a decade of trained-user habit. But the *direction* has changed. Total ending ARR growth guided to **10.2% for FY2026**, down from the mid-teens of FY2021–22, with management deliberately trading near-term ARR for AI monetization. Generative models (OpenAI, Google, Midjourney, Runway) and lower-cost design tools (Canva, Figma) attack the casual/prosumer tier — the seat-expansion engine. AI ARR has passed ~$500–650M, real but only ~2.5% of revenue and not yet proven to be incremental rather than cannibalizing credit-based upsell.

**Digital Experience — Weak.** Competing head-on with Salesforce, Microsoft, HubSpot in marketing automation. No durable pricing power. ~25% of revenue with structurally lower returns.

**Moat verdict:** the switching costs are real and the installed base is enormous, but the *sources* of the moat (per-seat pricing against headcount, professional tooling complexity) are precisely what AI compresses. A business whose returns on capital are this high but whose growth is decelerating into a technological shift gets **Narrow**, not Wide. This is the single most important judgment in the thesis, and it is why I do not call ADBE a "wonderful company at a fair price" without qualification.

**Evidence the moat is still functioning:** ROIC of **47.7%** in FY2025 (vs. ~32–33% in FY22–24) — rising, not falling; gross margin at a five-year high; revenue +12% in each of the last three reported quarters *while* the stock fell 31% YTD. Erosion shows up in the multiple, not yet in the P&L.
